title: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency & Secure SDLC — Compliance Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's operational controls, workflows, and evidence requirements for: RBAC and authentication; audit logging and log retention; data residency and retention policy; Secure SDLC controls; security-specific incident response steps; compliance evidence collection and review; and risk & exceptions handling. The document is intended for engineers, SREs, product security, and audit teams.

Goals and scope
- Provide clear ownership and actionable procedures that produce auditable evidence.
- Ensure RBAC decisions are consistent across cloud, console, and private deployments.
- Maintain tamper-evident audit logging with retention aligned to contractual and regulatory requirements.
- Integrate security checkpoints across the SDLC to prevent regressions and produce continuous evidence for assessments.

Owners and SLAs
- Policy owner: Security (Aisha Patel)
- Operational owner: Eng-SRE (Evan Carter)
- Evidence steward: Compliance (Priya Nair)
- Logging availability SLO: 99.9% delivery of security-relevant events to the central logging cluster within 5 minutes.
- Log integrity SLO: 100% daily checksums computed and verified, anomalies triaged within 24 hours.

1) RBAC and Authentication

Summary
We implement least privilege across all surfaces (Console, API, Private control plane, Dedicated clusters). RBAC is enforced using role templates and attribute-based rules. Authentication is federated (OIDC + SAML) for humans, and short-lived workload credentials for services.

Key concepts and components
- Identity providers: Okta (employees), Cloud IAM (service principals), Customer IdPs for Private deployments.
- Roles: Viewer, Developer, CI/CD, SRE, Platform-Admin, Security-Auditor, Compliance-ReadOnly, Customer-Admin (for private deployments).
- Role templates: stored in git (infra/iam/role-templates) and applied by terraform.

Permission matrix (examples)
| Role | Console actions | API keys | Secrets access | Audit view | Change approval |
|------|-----------------|----------|---------------|-----------|-----------------|
| Viewer | Read-only | No | No | Yes | No |
| Developer | Deploy non-prod services | Rotate own API keys | No | Yes | No |
| SRE | Runbooks, incidents | Create ephemeral service creds | Read-only secrets | Yes | Escalation only |
| Platform-Admin | Manage infra configs | Full | Encrypted access | Yes | Requires 2 approvers |
| Security-Auditor | Read-only across infra | No | No | Full | No |

Access request and approval workflow
1. Engineer opens an access request in Jira: component = iam-access, include justification and least-privilege scope.
2. IAM owner (Eng Infra) does automated policy simulation (terraform plan + policy-sim) and returns recommended role.
3. For elevated roles (Platform-Admin, Secrets access), require: manager approval + security approval.
4. Temporary access duration default: 8 hours. Long lived exceptions require documented risk exception (see section 7).

Automated guardrails
- Pull requests that modify role-templates must pass the iam-policy-checker (pre-merge).
- Changes that grant wildcards or broad read access trigger a blocking alert to security Slack channel #sec-iam.
- All privilege grants are logged to audit-log (see section 2).

2) Audit Logging and Retention

Logging scope
- Security-relevant events: auth success/failure, token creation/rotation, role changes, secret access, admin console actions, API key lifecycle events, data exports, and policy changes.
- Infrastructure telemetry: provisioning, scaling, kernel/runtime alerts for serving runtime.

Architecture
- Primary collectors: CloudTrail (cloud control plane), Internal audit endpoint (services push structured audit events), Fluentd -> central logging cluster (Elasticsearch/Opensearch or managed equivalent).
- Immutable storage: daily-encrypted S3 buckets with object-lock enabled (retention policies per data residency requirements).

Retention policy (default)
| Event type | Retention (hosted) | Retention (customer private) | Evidence tag |
|------------|-------------------|-----------------------------|-------------|
| Auth events | 2 years | Customer-configurable (min 90 days) | auth-logs |
| Role changes | 7 years | Customer-configurable | iam-audit |
| Secret access traces | 1 year | Customer-configurable | secrets-audit |
| Data exports | 7 years | Customer-configurable | export-audit |

Log integrity and monitoring
- Daily checksum and HMAC verification against stored manifests.
- Siem rules: abnormal privilege escalations, multiple failed auths from new geos, large data export events.
- Pager escalation: security-oncall if critical SIEM rule triggers.

Compliance evidence generation
- Evidence package = zipped manifests + signed checksums + event query snapshots + runbook that produced the logs. Compliance steward runs evidence extraction using the compliance-cli:

Example: extract auth events for audit window
compliance-cli extract --type auth-logs --start 2026-10-01 --end 2026-10-31 --owner security --output /tmp/oct-auth-evidence.zip

3) Data Residency and Retention Controls

Principles
- Follow customer contractual requirements and applicable laws (GDPR, CCPA, sector regs).
- Default hosted storage regions: us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Customer-specific residency options require Private deployment or dedicated region.

Process for data locality requests
1. Customer requests residency during onboarding; Sales records in contract metadata the region requirements.
2. Onboarding runbook (see related_pages) provisions tenant with region-scoped storage and encryption keys.
3. Proof: provide signed manifest showing storage buckets and KMS key ARNs.

Retention lifecycle
- Retention is split by data class (PII, usage telemetry, debug traces).
- Deletion workflow: async job that replaces object with tombstone, then purges after retention window. Purge must be irreversible and logged.

Retention table (examples)
| Data class | Hosted default | Customer-mandated min |
|------------|----------------|----------------------|
| PII (identified) | 1 year | 90 days |
| Aggregated telemetry | 2 years | 1 year |
| Debug traces (KV cache) | 90 days | 30 days |

4) Secure SDLC (Policy + Gateways)

Goals
- Shift-left security: static analysis, dependency checks, secret scanning, and infra policy validation persistently in CI.
- Produce checklistable evidence for every release.

Required CI gates
- Unit tests and integration tests (required).
- SAST (bandit/semgrep or equivalent) with no critical findings.
- Dependency scanning (OWASP dependency-check / Snyk) with no critical vulnerabilities.
- Secret scanning (git-secrets + pre-commit) blocking.
- Terraform plan + drift checks + iam-policy-checker for infra changes.
- Security review for changes touching: auth, RBAC, secrets, export flows.

Release artifact evidence
- CI run IDs, artifact checksums, SAST report IDs, dependency scan snapshots, terraform plan diffs. The release bundle must include a manifest.json listing these artifacts for the release. Compliance CLI can generate an evidence bundle:

Example manifest snippet
{
  "release_id": "2026.11.15-rc2",
  "artifacts": ["artifact-sha256:...","sast-report-id:...","tf-plan-id:..."]
}

5) Incident Response (security-specific procedures)

Purpose
Integrate security controls into the incident lifecycle to ensure forensic readiness, minimal data exposure, and timely communication to stakeholders.

Security triage checklist (first 60 minutes)
1. Triage owner (oncall SRE) tags incident P0/P1.
2. Security oncall (pager) joins within 15 minutes.
3. Capture forensic snapshot: preserve impacted VM/container images, central logs for relevant time window, and network flow captures.
4. Rotate credentials that may be impacted (API keys, service accounts).
5. If data exfiltration suspected, enact containment: disable external egress for affected service, enable enhanced logging, and preserve evidence.

Forensics and evidence handling
- Evidence chain of custody: document who accessed the evidence, timestamps, and storage location.
- Hash artifacts and store checksums in evidence-bucket with object-lock.

Communication and legal
- Security lead coordinates legal and privacy to evaluate notification obligations.
- Customer-facing communications are approved by legal + customer success.

Post-incident review
- Postmortem must include: timeline, root cause, mitigations, ATT&CK mapping, evidence package id, and risk re-assessment. Postmortems are linked to the evidence package for audit.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Quarterly readiness and ad-hoc audit process
- Quarterly: Compliance runs full evidence extraction for a random sample of controls and verifies signatures and manifests.
- Ad-hoc: On audit request, generate an evidence package within 7 business days for standard SOC2-style requests. High-priority customers may require 3 business day turnaround (contractual).

Evidence package contents
- Control mapping index (control -> evidence artifacts)
- Artifact manifests (checksums + provenance)
- Query snapshots (SIEM queries and results)
- Release artifact manifest (see section 4)
- Signed statements from owners (security, eng-sre, product)

Example CLI: generate package for control AC-6 (RBAC review)
compliance-cli package --control AC-6 --period 2026-Q3 --output /tmp/AC6-Q3-evidence.zip

7) Risk and Exceptions

Acceptable exception criteria
- Exceptions must have documented business justification, technical mitigation, and defined compensating controls.
- Maximum exception duration: 90 days. Extensions require elevated review (Security Director + Head of Product).

Exception request workflow
1. Engineer opens a Jira ticket with component=security-exception and attaches a filled risk template.
2. Security performs risk assessment: likelihood, impact, compensating controls, and recommended mitigations.
3. If approved, create exception record in the exceptions register, include reviewer signatures, and schedule re-evaluation 7 days before expiry.

Template fields (example)
- Requestor: name and team
- Affected resource(s): cloud account, service, secret id
- Business justification
- Expected duration
- Compensating controls
- Evidence to be produced during exception window

8) Auditable artifacts and retention for the playbook
- All role-template PRs and approvals (git + CI logs) retained for 7 years.
- Evidence packages retain manifest + checksums for configured retention period (see section 2).
- Incident evidence and postmortems retained 7 years.

- iam-policy-checker (terraform plan analysis)
- log-query examples (Opensearch DSL snippets)
